\section*{AP \({ }^{\text {® }}\) CALCULUS AB \\ 2011 SCORING GUIDELINES (Form B)}

\section*{Question 4}

Consider a differentiable function \(f\) having domain all positive real numbers, and for which it is known that \(f^{\prime}(x)=(4-x) x^{-3}\) for \(x>0\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the \(x\)-coordinate of the critical point of \(f\). Determine whether the point is a relative maximum, a relative minimum, or neither for the function \(f\). Justify your answer.
\item[(b)] Find all intervals on which the graph of \(f\) is concave down. Justify your answer.
\item[(c)] Given that \(f(1)=2\), determine the function \(f\).
\item[(a)] \(f^{\prime}(x)=0\) at \(x=4\)
\(f^{\prime}(x)>0\) for \(0<x<4\)
\(f^{\prime}(x)<0\) for \(x>4\)
Therefore \(f\) has a relative maximum at \(x=4\).
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: x=4 \\ 1: \text { relative maximum } \\ 1: \text { justification }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[(b)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
f^{\prime \prime}(x) & =-x^{-3}+(4-x)\left(-3 x^{-4}\right) \\
& =-x^{-3}-12 x^{-4}+3 x^{-3} \\
& =2 x^{-4}(x-6) \\
& =\frac{2(x-6)}{x^{4}} \\
f^{\prime \prime}(x) & <0 \text { for } 0<x<6
\end{aligned}
\]
The graph of \(f\) is concave down on the interval \(0<x<6\).
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}2: f^{\prime \prime}(x) \\ 1: \text { answer with justification }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[(c)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(x) & =2+\int_{1}^{x}\left(4 t^{-3}-t^{-2}\right) d t \\
& =2+\left[-2 t^{-2}+t^{-1}\right]_{t=1}^{t=x} \\
& =3-2 x^{-2}+x^{-1}
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { integral } \\ 1: \text { antiderivative } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\end{itemize}
